qs.q:
Match each message (1–5) and its meaning (A–F).
There is one letter that you do not need.

0. I haven't heard from you in ages. Is everything okay? [G = How are you?]
1. You may want to consider the options you've got carefully. At this point in life you can't afford to make another mistake, as it could really cost you.
2. You've obviously had a hard time recently, so why don't you take your mind off it and just relax a bit. Let somebody else make the choice. I'd be happy to do it for you.
3. If you thought things through carefully, you wouldn't be in this position now. Just accept it.
4. I know you've been under a lot of pressure lately and it's a tough choice for sure, but I don't think I can wait for your response any longer.
5. It couldn't be prevented, no matter what you say. I realise you're worried about it constantly, but you can get over it. Time fixes everything.
items: 1 — You can't afford to make another mistake. It could really cost you.
2 — Take your mind off it and relax. I'd be happy to make the choice for you.
3 — If you'd thought carefully, you wouldn't be in this position. Just accept it.
4 — It's a tough choice but I can't wait for your response any longer.
5 — It couldn't be prevented. You can get over it. Time fixes everything.
rights: A — You need to make up your mind.
B — It's time to face the consequences.
C — You can leave this decision to me.
D — Things will work out for you eventually.
E — You'll get your answer as soon as possible.
F — Think twice before you make your next move.

What do Ben and Greta need to discuss?

"Thanks for suggesting we take a break in July and go sailing. It'll be more challenging than last year. In the meantime, I've noticed your efforts are no longer appreciated at the office, so maybe you should start looking for something else. We can go through the options when we meet on Friday. I'll book us a table at the Asian restaurant."

A A job change.
B Going out for a meal.
C The upcoming holidays.

How does Paul feel about the visit to the zoo?

"We're going to the zoo this weekend. The plan was to do the Canopy Walk, but Mona and I will pass since we have a problem with heights. We'll spend all our time watching the animals at ground level and trying not to disturb them. Can't wait."

A He is worried about it.
B He doesn't want to go.
C He is looking forward to it.
opts: He is looking forward to it.

Read the message from Peter:

"Hello!
My parents want me to clean my room and do other household chores regularly.
So I wonder what you have to do at home and why?
When did you start doing household chores and how did you learn to do them?
What is your favourite obligation at home and why?
Peter"

Write Peter a reply. Answer all his questions. Write 80–100 words.

You will hear five voice messages.
Match each message (1–5) and its meaning (A–F).
There is one letter that you do not need.

A — Help me.
B — I'd like to pay.
C — Please find it.
D — It's too expensive.
E — I haven't got it yet.
F — I don't need your help.
rights: E — I haven't got it yet.
F — I don't need your help.
